subject: german
title: Stamp 1: Social Media in Germany
welcome_lead: Stamp the role of social media in modern German society.
meta_desc: A-Level German adventure on social media, digital society, and online discourse in Germany.

concepts.def: Social media; platforms like Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X.
Digitalisation; transformation of work, education, and administration through digital tools.
Filter bubble; algorithmically narrowed exposure to information.
Cyberbullying; harassment via digital platforms, especially among young people.
Person who builds reach and influence through social platforms.
Youth media use; tracked annually by the JIM study (around 4 hours per day online).

walkthroughs.body_html: YouTube, WhatsApp, Instagram, and TikTok dominate younger users. Older users still use Facebook. X and BlueSky host political debate. Each platform creates its own dynamics and risks.
The annual JIM-Studie (Jugend, Information, Medien) tracks 12-19 year olds. Smartphone ownership is near 100%; daily internet use averages around four hours, mainly via messaging and video.
Benefits include access to information and community; risks include Cybermobbing, Hassrede, screen-time effects, and addiction. Schools introduce media literacy (Medienkompetenz) programmes.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I use my phone every day' in German?
options: Ich nutze mein Telefon jeden Tag.
Ich benutze mein Handy jeden Tag.
Ich gehe Kaffee trinken morgen.
Ich gebrauche mein Phone jeden Tag.

mcqs.q: When does 'in' take the accusative vs dative?
options: Accusative for movement INTO a place; dative for location IN a place.
It always takes the same case.
Ich gehe Kaffee trinken morgen.
It depends on the speaker's mood.
